page: Microsoft Azure D48_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dv4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with 24 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz and is equipped with 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX512_VNNI, alongside AES cryptography and virtualization extensions. The instance is configured with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It contains no local storage and does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the D48_v4 delivers average multi-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by its stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. However, its single-core performance is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng single-core tests. Memory performance is generally solid, with average read-only bandwidth and strong write bandwidth for large uncached blocks. The server exhibits average capabilities in tasks such as software compilation, image processing, and database operations. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in large language model inference; while prompt processing speeds for small and medium models are average, text generation speeds are poor, falling into the bottom 10%.

From a cost efficiency perspective, the D48_v4 provides a balanced resource profile suitable for enterprise workloads that require substantial memory and multi-core processing without the added cost of local storage or GPU hardware. Given its hardware specifications and benchmark results, this server is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, software compilation, and standard database operations. It is less appropriate for single-threaded tasks or real-time LLM text generation due to its weaker single-core and text generation performance.
